health.name: health
health.usageInstructions:
### Health
Injury capacity. Deduct only when a blow, fall, burn, blast or Quirk effect actually injures the character.
### Deduct
- Minor injury (bruise, shallow cut, light burn): 5-15% of maximum
- Serious injury (broken bone, deep wound, heavy burn): 15-35% of maximum
- Near-fatal injury: down to 1-10% of maximum
Quirk backlash at Quirk Strain 100 counts as a serious injury.
### Do not deduct when
- Anything for a classmate's Quirk use in a test or drill that is not a fight (the Quirk Apprehension Test, fitness tests, races, drills): nobody is hurt by another student there
- More than a minor injury for a classmate's accident in supervised sparring or a battle exercise (a stray beam, a wild throw, a misjudged landing): it is a minor injury at most, and the teacher stops anything worse
- More than a minor injury for a classmate's accident in supervised training or a test (a stray beam, a wild throw, a misjudged landing): it is a minor injury at most, and the teacher stops anything worse
- An existing injury is described again or hurts on movement
- The character is unconscious, carried or under treatment
- The scene is dangerous but nothing has hit them yet
- A teacher or referee stops a training bout before the blow lands
### Recovery
Field first aid (a first aid kit, bandages, a splint, a trained classmate) restores about 10% of maximum health once per injury and stops bleeding; it does not mend bones. No regeneration per turn. A full rest restores a quarter of the maximum. Recovery Girl's healing restores up to half of the maximum at once but spends the patient's stamina; a patient with little stamina heals less and must sleep it off. Serious injuries continue in hospital care over days.
### At 0
The character is down: unconscious or unable to act. Defeat leads to rescue, capture or hospital care, never an invented death.

stamina.name: stamina
stamina.usageInstructions:
### Stamina
Bodily exertion. Walking, talking, lectures and ordinary work cost 0.
### Deduct once per action
- Brief effort (a sprint, a hard strike, a vault): 3
- Demanding effort (a technique, a long climb, a heavy lift): 6
- Heavy effort (a rescue carry, a long exchange of blows, a big push): 12
- Extreme effort (a burst at the body's limit): 20
Techniques state their cost.
### Do not deduct when
- A Quirk is used: that raises Quirk Strain instead, unless the character's Drawback says otherwise
- An action is planned, discussed or watched
### Recovery
Returns 5 per turn of light activity and fully after a night's sleep. Recovery Girl's healing spends the patient's stamina. Low stamina limits the body: heavy and extreme efforts fail or cost health.

Quirk Strain.name: Quirk Strain
Quirk Strain.usageInstructions:
### Quirk Strain
How hard the character has pushed their own Quirk. Starts at 0, rises with active use and falls by 4 every turn on its own. Quirkless characters never gain Strain.
### Add once per use
- Light (a small or practiced use): +5
- Moderate (a standard technique or sustained use): +8
- Heavy (a big technique, pushing range or force): +15
- Severe (an ultimate move or going past a known limit): +25
Techniques state their Strain. Add half for an Exceptional Quirk; halve it for a Developing Quirk. Growth: a technique the story has trained, or one used many times, costs one level less (Severe as Heavy, Heavy as Moderate, Moderate as Light).
### Flight and movement
- Flying at an easy pace with wings or a practiced movement Quirk: Light, once per flight, not every turn
- Fast maneuvers, a dive, carrying someone or fighting in the air: Moderate
- Top speed or flying past a known limit: Heavy or Severe
- One action or one turn never adds more than +25 in total (+37 for an Exceptional Quirk); a custom technique adds what its own rating says, once.
### Do not add when
- The Quirk is mentioned, planned, watched or discussed
- A Mutant's permanent features are used for ordinary living: a casual flap, folding or stretching wings, a tail swish, gliding or hovering in place
- Someone else's Quirk acts on the character
- The character rests, waits, talks or lets someone else act this turn: Strain only falls, never rises (Gifted Quirks still held active are the only exception)
- A use already counted on an earlier turn: each use is added once
- A use the character's Quirk rules mark "Strain: none" or costing nothing (staying invisible, ordinary running on engines, regenerating at normal pace, daily use of an always-on body)
### More than one Quirk
- Fusion Quirk: it is one Quirk; each technique states its own Strain, and mixing both natures outside a technique costs one level more.
- Gifted Quirks: two Quirks in one action cost both and +10; three cost all three and +25; holding two or more active adds +5 every turn they stay on.
### Thresholds
- Below 60: nothing a teacher would notice, and no injury. Until the Drawback's first threshold (60, or 50 for an Exceptional Quirk) there are no symptoms of any kind: no stinging, aching, headache or shaking.
- 60 or more: the character's Drawback starts to show, in that Drawback's own way and no other; describe it, but it hurts no one.
- 80 or more: the Drawback is active; a failed use beyond a light one may hurt the user.
- 100: the Quirk gives out (a minor injury at most); no further use until Strain falls below 60.
### Recovery
Falls 4 per turn. A full night's sleep or a long rest clears it: subtract what remains. Recovery Girl's healing does not clear Strain.
